problem: VLM-based navigators only do passive obstacle avoidance and act as semantic reasoners with no grasp of the robot's physical skill limits, so they cannot decide when to interact with objects or which object to move to clear a blocked path. Classical NAMO methods need global maps and simple geometry.
motivation: Cluttered homes and disaster sites often have no collision-free path, so the robot must physically reconfigure the scene. Planning here needs causal reasoning about how removing an object changes goal reachability, plus metric-aware knowledge of what the embodiment can traverse or manipulate.
key_idea: Fine-tune a VLM on counterfactual-reasoning-derived VQA data, with parametric skill constraints injected in the prompt and grounded in a metric traversability map, and pair it with an RL skill library including a traversability-oriented pushing policy.
insight: Distilling offline counterfactual path-length gain (A* with and without an object) into the VLM lets it decide interaction necessity and target from a single RGB image, without online simulation. Removing fine-tuning drops SR from 0.68 to 0.17, and replacing the traversability-oriented manipulation (TOM) policy with a two-stage relocate-then-navigate scheme drops SR to 0.53 with longer paths. Accuracy differences by embodiment show the model conditions its decisions on the injected skill constraints.
method: Skill-aware VLM input: the prompt carries the skill set plus parametric constraints (traversal height, clearance width, manipulable categories, reach range), and the model outputs a skill and, if it is an interaction skill, a target object.

Metric-scale grounding: VGGT relative depth is rescaled by the median ratio to Map-Anything metric depth, back-projected, and ground-aligned with Grounding DINO plus RANSAC. A height threshold h_max and inflation by the clearance radius give a traversability map; Grounding DINO detections are checked against the manipulation workspace.

Counterfactual data labeling: for sampled goals, A* runs on M_trav and on M_trav^{-o} with object o's point cloud removed (SAM2 masks). The gain G(o)=1-l(M^{-o})/l(M) is computed and the argmax object is chosen if the gain exceeds a threshold epsilon.
VQA generation with introspective CoT: about 20K samples whose reasoning has a skill-feasibility check followed by an interaction-necessity rationale; SFT of Qwen3-VL with next-token loss.
Whole-body low-level controller: PPO policy taking base velocity and end-effector pose commands and outputting 18-DoF joint targets (Go2 legs + ARX5 arm).

Traversability-oriented manipulation skill: robot-centric PPO policy rewarded for reaching a goal location (r_nav+r_safe+r_eff), with contact points sampled from the object surface and randomized boxes, buckets and chairs. It pushes just enough to clear the path.
Door-opening skill and navigation skill: a PPO door skill with handle/hinge keypoints from Molmo, and an A*+pure-pursuit navigation skill. Execution parameters come from SAM2 masks and metric depth.

setting.backbone: Qwen3-VL-8B (fine-tuned) as high-level reasoner; PPO RL policies for low-level and skills
setting.training_data: About 20K VQA samples generated in Isaac Sim on Matterport3D layouts populated with interactive assets (90/10 train/test split); RL skills trained in Isaac Lab in simulation
setting.observation: egocentric monocular RGB (VLM) plus depth/LiDAR local map and robot pose for the low-level stack
setting.action_space: high-level skill choice (navigate / manipulate object / open door) plus target pixel; low-level base velocity + end-effector pose -> 18-DoF joint position targets
setting.privileged: Robot pose assumed; no global map. GT object states are given to the RL policy in the simulation baseline comparison; door models are simplified.

numbers.eval_set_note: 150 episodes, 15 scenes (small room, big room, room-to-room), 10 start-goal pairs each; the paper states 50 episodes per scenario type
numbers.extra: Unitree Go2 + ARX5 in Isaac Sim; single run; GT object states for RL policy observations
numbers.evidence: Table tab:sim_results, Average column, CoINS row

numbers.extra: ablation subset; w/o fine-tuning SR 0.17, w/o TOM SR 0.53

numbers.eval_set_note: 10% held-out VQA test set; skill+object selection accuracy

numbers_note: Results are on the authors' own Isaac Sim benchmark; SR is printed as a fraction (0.75). Real-world results are qualitative only.
results: CoINS reaches average SR 0.75, PL 10.32 m and DTG 1.19 m, beating IN-Sight (0.64 SR, 1.96 DTG) and IN-ArmPush (0.55). The gap is largest in room-to-room (0.58 vs 0.32 for IN-Sight). InterNav-VLM reaches 78.35% reasoning accuracy against Gemini-2.5-Pro at 58.34% and GPT-4o at 48.64%.
limitations: VLM reasoning errors from a single RGB view (unnecessary interaction, omitted prerequisite interaction, wrong skill) and skill execution failures (collisions, failure to clear the path).
Simplified doors without handle manipulation; only pushing skills; evaluation is small-scale (150 episodes) on a self-built benchmark with a single run.
No memory or long-horizon reasoning and limited 3D spatial understanding; skills rely on GT object states in training and on a perception pipeline at test time.
